title: MedSync clerking history catalogue
status: DRAFT for CSO sign-off (GATE A). No item is clinically live until signed.
scope: Adult history-taking (patients aged 16 and over): presenting complaint, history, review of systems, past history (conditions, operations, transfusions, medicines, allergies), family and social history. Examination, paediatrics and obstetrics are separate catalogues.

conventions.ids: Stable snake_case ids. Symptoms are prefixed 'sym.'. The app stores ids, never display labels.
conventions.answer_states: Each symptom in review of systems is yes, no or not asked. 'Not asked' is never written into the note as a negative.
conventions.properties: kind: one (single choice), many (multiple; exclusive_options clear the others), count (stepper), scale (0 to 10), duration (value plus unit), text.
conventions.phrases: phrase.pre and phrase.post build the sentence clause for a property.
conventions.sensitivity: standard, or a restricted class (hiv, tb, mental_health, sexual_reproductive_health). Restricted items carry a lock and never appear in patient-facing text.
conventions.local_terms: Empty on purpose. Ugandan clinicians supply local-language terms; nothing is machine-translated.
conventions.sex: applies_to_sex null means everyone; 'female' or 'male' hides the item for other recorded sexes.

review_of_systems.nothing_else: Answers every still-unasked, non-linked item in that system as no, in one tap.

linked_answers.principle: A symptom recorded in Complaint shows as a linked 'yes' in the review of systems and cannot be answered there. Associated options whose id is a symptom id also create linked answers. Red-flag answers of 'no' that name a symptom create linked 'no' answers.

rules.sets: a red flag whose id matches a symptom's id sets that symptom yes or no

flag_levels.display: Badges appear only in the Flags panel in the right-hand column. Badge text is symptom words only: no level words, no 'red flag' prefix. Badges with the same text merge; the most severe level wins; the hover text lists every reason and where it came from.

associated_count_gte_ref with 'among_groups' (each group counts once; a group item may require a property)
flag_rule_language.applies_to: a symptom id, a list of symptom ids, 'family:<family>', 'any', or a record ('medicines', 'allergies', 'vital_signs').
flag_rule_language.numbers: Every threshold is a reference entry (REF-FLAG-*). A rule whose reference is unsigned does not fire.

flag_rules.reason: Chest pain with features of acute coronary syndrome, current or within 12 hours: emergency assessment
flag_rules.note: Pain lasting over 15 minutes is an ACS feature on its own; severity is not a criterion.

flag_rules.reason: Chest pain with ACS features 12 to 72 hours ago: same-day assessment
Sudden tearing or sharp chest pain, or pain going through to the back: exclude aortic dissection
Chest pain worse on breathing in, with breathlessness or coughing blood: consider pulmonary embolism
Sudden-onset breathlessness: consider pulmonary embolism
One swollen painful leg with breathlessness: consider pulmonary embolism
Fever with a danger sign: assess for severe malaria, sepsis or meningitis now
Abdominal pain with features of an acute abdomen or bleeding
Vomit containing blood or coffee grounds: upper gastrointestinal bleeding
Faeculent vomiting: bowel obstruction
Black tarry stools or heavy rectal bleeding
Swelling of lips, tongue or face with breathing difficulty, wheeze, hoarseness or collapse: possible anaphylaxis
Swelling of lips, tongue or face without airway features
Headache with a red-flag feature
Back pain with a cauda equina red flag
flag_rules.note: Any one of these is enough; the earlier prototype rule needing two was wrong.

flag_rules.reason: Blackout with a cardiac red flag: urgent cardiovascular assessment
Sudden weakness, numbness or speech change: possible stroke
Sudden weakness, numbness or speech change that has resolved: possible TIA, assess today
Upper gastrointestinal bleeding
Black, tarry stools: possible upper gastrointestinal bleeding
flag_rules.note: Iron gives dark green-black, not tarry, stools; taking iron never switches this off.

flag_rules.reason: Large-volume haemoptysis
Fever with an exposure: screen for viral haemorrhagic fever and isolate
flag_rules.note: Bleeding is not required: in the 2026 Bundibugyo outbreak only 3 of 18 admitted patients bled.

flag_rules.reason: Fever with at least three case-definition symptoms during a declared outbreak
flag_rules.note: Only while the hospital's outbreak mode is on; set by the IPC focal person. Each group counts once, as in the WHO list (aching muscles or joints is one item; vomiting, not nausea).

flag_rules.reason: Unexplained bleeding during a declared outbreak: screen for viral haemorrhagic fever
Thoughts of self-harm: assess safety today
Polyuria with vomiting, abdominal pain, drowsiness or fast breathing: possible hyperglycaemic emergency; check glucose and ketones
Sudden scrotal pain: possible torsion
Red eye with vision change, light sensitivity or an injury
Sore throat with drooling or noisy breathing: airway risk
Breathless at rest or speaking in words only
New or worsening confusion (scores 3 in NEWS2)

diabetes.composer_rule: A clause whose property is unanswered is omitted with its punctuation. An unanswered property is an absent key and leaves no mark in the note.
diabetes.rule: Reported, not verified. Nothing here is charted; the type and the complications become qualifiers on the problem-list proposal the clinician confirms.
diabetes.not_here: Gestational diabetes in a previous pregnancy is NOT an option under 'type': it would make the woman a known diabetic to every rule. It is a separate past-history question (below), a risk factor, and its restricted class is D-DM-30.

medicines.note: Doses are recorded as the patient or packet states; MedSync never suggests a dose here. Prescribing uses lib/prescribing and is out of scope.

allergies.note: Writes to the single allergy record (D-EMR-04). Uncoded names stay displayed and are flagged as not checked by prescribing.

family_history.note: Stored as conditions with subject_relation (Clinical Fact Contract).

alcohol.note: Local drink names to be confirmed by Ugandan clinicians; AUDIT-C can be added later.

occupation.note: Occupation shapes exposure risk (fishing and schistosomiasis, mining and TB or silicosis, health work and VHF).

composer.principle: The note text is assembled from structured answers by fixed rules (no AI). The clinician edits it before signing.
rules: One sentence per complaint: '{label} for {duration}, {onset} onset and {course}.' then one clause per answered property using its phrase pre/post.
Pain uses SOCRATES order: site; character; radiation ('does not radiate' for Nowhere); timing; aggravation; relief ('nothing eases it' for Nothing); severity 'n out of 10'.
Red flags: 'Red flags present: a; b.' then 'Absent: c; d.' Only answered items appear.

Review of systems: positives by system with their detail sentences; systems fully answered no become 'No {system} symptoms.'; partly answered systems list their no answers; unanswered systems appear under 'Not reviewed:'.
Linked answers are not repeated in the review of systems text.
Restricted items appear in the clinical note only; the patient-facing summary excludes them (D-EMR-13).
Numbers are written as digits with units; options are lower-cased mid-sentence except proper nouns and abbreviations.
